papers.title_in_file: Scaling Quantum Machine Learning without Tricks: Full-Resolution and Diverse Image Generation
papers.what_it_is: Simulated end-to-end quantum Wasserstein GANs trained on full MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, compared by FID with a patch-based QGAN and a classical GAN benchmark.

assertions.value: The authors report an FID of 152 on 3-class MNIST against 207 for the patch-QGAN of Tsang et al., and an FID of 60 on 2-class Fashion-MNIST against 179.
quotes: On the 3-class MNIST, our QGAN achieves an FID of 152, improving upon the patch-QGAN (FID 207). On the 2-class Fashion-MNIST, our model reaches an FID of 60, substantially outperforming the patch-QGAN result of 179.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single study, FID comparison on the authors' own runs against published patch-QGAN numbers.

assertions.value: The authors report FIDs of 109 on MNIST and 70 on Fashion-MNIST for their QGAN, and cite classical Wasserstein GAN mean FIDs of approximately 55 for MNIST and 85 for Fashion-MNIST from a benchmark study.
quotes: In comparison, our QGAN can achieve FIDs of 109 on MNIST and 70 on Fashion-MNIST, which is higher (worse) for MNIST
mean FIDs of approximately 55 for MNIST and 85 for Fashion-MNIST are reported
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; classical figures are cited from Lucic et al., with no extensive hyperparameter search on the quantum side.
assertions.reader_inference: The QGAN is worse than the classical mean on MNIST and better on Fashion-MNIST; the authors do not tune hyperparameters.

assertions.value: The authors state that outperforming classical approaches and demonstrating quantum advantage are not direct goals, and that they claim no exponential quantum speedup from the encoding or measurement process.
quotes: neither outperforming classical approaches nor demonstrating quantum advantage is a direct goal
We neither claim nor imply any exponential quantum speedup arising from the encoding or measurement process.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in Sec. V, p.12.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum classical hybrid neural networks for continuous variable prediction
papers.what_it_is: Simulated hybrid quantum-classical and photonic neural networks predicting Boston housing prices.

assertions.value: The authors report that the hybrid quantum neural network performed slightly better than a simple classical neural network with the same settings, and took about three times the time to train.
quotes: First Quantum Neural network model performs slightly better than the simple classical neural network with the same settings & configurations though it took about three times the time to train compared to the classical NN
assertions.certainty_reason: Single simulated experiment on one small dataset, assessed from loss curves.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper gives no statistical test; the comparison rests on loss-decay plots.

assertions.value: The authors report that the photonic quantum network was limited to 3 features by simulation cost and pretty much did not learn anything.
quotes: for the simulation purpose finally 3 features were used for training, which took around two hours to train & as expected the model pretty much did not learn anything.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single simulated run; the authors attribute the result to the small number of features.

assertions.value: The authors use the Boston Housing dataset of 506 samples, reduced by PCA to 9 principal components to reach 95% of explained variance, and run on a simulator.
quotes: The dataset has total 506 samples.
Here we can see that to get at-least 95% of variance explained we need 9 principal components.
results from a very simple QNN trained on a simulator
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own dataset and setup in Sec. 4.

papers.title_in_file: Validation and benchmarking of quantum annealing technology (doctoral dissertation)
papers.what_it_is: A doctoral dissertation benchmarking D-Wave quantum annealers on quantum dynamics simulation and railway conflict management, with two classical Ising solvers.

assertions.value: The author reports that present-day D-Wave annealers can capture the dynamics of a very simple two-level system, and that several classical solvers perform better than the tested quantum devices.
quotes: our experiments indicated that already the present-day D-Wave annealers can capture the dynamics of a very simple two-level system.
concluding that they perform better than the tested quantum devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: Experimental result from one thesis on specific D-Wave devices.

assertions.value: The author reports that D-Wave annealers found an optimal solution to the small railway problem instances, with performance varying greatly with annealing time and chain strength.
quotes: were able to successfully find an optimal solution to the small problem instances, although the performance varied greatly depending on the parameters such as the annealing time and chain strength.
assertions.certainty_reason: Experiments on two Polish railway segments with two annealer generations.

assertions.value: The author states that the applicability of the dynamics algorithm to current devices is limited by their small number of qubits and sparse connectivity, and that the current annealer generation is far from perfect, with instances where the annealers failed to find a good or even feasible solution.
quotes: Although the applicability of the algorithm to current devices is limited by their small number of qubits and sparse connectivity
generation of the D-Wave annealers is far from perfect. We discuss problem instances for which the annealers failed to find a good or even feasible solution.
assertions.certainty_reason: The thesis states these limits in its Abstract and Summary.

papers.title_in_file: Adaptive Relational Learning on Multi-instance Quantum Data with Photonic Processors
papers.what_it_is: A numerical study of an adaptive relational QML model using Bargmann invariants on photonic continuous-variable data, benchmarked against classical shadows.

assertions.value: The authors report perfect test accuracy already for n = 2 and 100 times fewer shots per data point than the shadow-based method.
quotes: Already for n = 2, we achieve perfect test accuracy
while using 100 times fewer shots per data point
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result from one study on the authors' chosen tasks.

assertions.value: The authors state that the cost of shadow estimation grows rapidly with n while their model avoids this dependence.
quotes: show that the cost of shadow estimation grows rapidly with n, while our model avoids this dependence.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' result for their chosen observables; not a general proof in the abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that their results are numerical and that they provide a mapping onto a programmable time-bin photonic architecture as a route toward experimental implementation.
quotes: Already in the simplest two-state setting, our numerical results demonstrated an orders-of-magnitude reduction in the required shot budget for the adaptive approach.
providing a concrete route toward experimental implementation.
assertions.certainty_reason: The conclusion states the scope as numerical plus a blueprint.

papers.what_it_is: A theory paper defining shadow models (quantum-trained, classically deployed) and proving a learning separation and limits.

assertions.value: The paper proves, under the hardness of classically computing the discrete cube root, a learning task where a shadow model trained on a quantum computer and evaluated classically achieves arbitrarily good performance while any fully classical model does no significantly better than random guessing.
quotes: There exists a learning task where a shadow model first trained using a quantum computer then evaluated classically on new input data, can achieve an arbitrarily good learning performance, while any fully classical model cannot do significantly better than random guessing, under the hardness of classically computing the discrete cube root.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1 (informal statement), with proof in the Appendix.

assertions.value: The paper proves that, assuming BQP is not contained in P/poly, there exist quantum models in BQP that are not shadowfiable.
quotes: Under the assumption that BQP
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 5, conditional on a complexity assumption.

assertions.value: The authors state that their trap-door function example remains somewhat contrived.
quotes: The example we presented, based on trap-door functions, readily allows for such constructions, but it remains somewhat contrived.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the Discussion, Sec. IV.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Review
papers.what_it_is: A review that defines quantum deep learning, gives a four-paradigm taxonomy, and assesses advantage claims, bottlenecks and a roadmap.

assertions.value: The authors define quantum deep learning and introduce a taxonomy of four primary paradigms: hybrid quantum-classical models, quantum deep neural networks, quantum algorithms for deep learning primitives, and quantum-inspired classical algorithms.
quotes: introduces a taxonomy comprising four primary paradigms: hybrid quantum-classical models, quantum deep neural networks, quantum algorithms for deep learning primitives, and quantum-inspired classical algorithms.
assertions.certainty_reason: The review's own definition and taxonomy, stated in the Abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that the structural restrictions that improve trainability can also move a quantum model toward regimes that admit efficient classical simulation.
quotes: the same structural restrictions that improve trainability can also move a quantum model toward regimes that admit efficient classical simulation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Review synthesis of cited literature, not a result of the review itself.

assertions.value: The authors state that the open question in QDL is whether a practical quantum advantage can be demonstrated and certified under realistic end-to-end constraints.
quotes: The open question in QDL is whether a practical quantum advantage can be demonstrated and certified under realistic
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' framing of the state of the field.

papers.title_in_file: Probabilistic Design of Parametrized Quantum Circuits through Local Gate Modifications
papers.what_it_is: A local quantum architecture search algorithm (LQAS) for parametrized circuits, tested on two synthetic and two quantum chemistry regression tasks with simulation and hardware runs.

assertions.value: The authors report that for one circuit the base R2 improved from -0.993 to 0.958 by the final LQAS iteration on the one-dimensional noisy quadratic dataset.
quotes: the base R2 was improved from -0.993 to 0.958 by the final LQAS iteration.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single simulated example on a synthetic dataset.

assertions.value: The authors state that model performance on real quantum hardware is lacking relative to state-vector simulation even with circuit optimization and error mitigation.
quotes: Another drawback is that even when circuit optimization and error mitigation is applied, model performance is lacking with respect to state-vector simulations.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' observation from their own hardware runs.

assertions.value: The authors state that the DDCC dataset can be modeled using PQCs with a few qubits, whereas wider circuits, more features and more model parameters are required for the BSE49 dataset.
quotes: the DDCC dataset is capable of being modeled using PQCs with a few qubits, whereas wider circuits, more features, and more model parameters are required to adequately model the BSE49 dataset.
assertions.certainty_reason: State-vector results on two datasets.
